subject: Hosted API: Data residency, retention and deletion — security questionnaire responses
messages:
From: Julia Santos <j.santos@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: security-team@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-14T09:12:23Z
Subject: Redwood Hosted API — data handling questionnaire

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our security review, we've attached a short questionnaire focused on data residency, retention, and deletion for Redwood's hosted API. Can you confirm the canonical answers for the questions below and return the completed sheet? We need clear statements for:

1) Where customer request/response data is stored (region options and defaults).
2) Default retention windows for input/output content, request metadata, and debug logs.
3) Mechanism and timeline for deletion-on-request (both account-level and one-off records).
4) How backups/snapshots are handled and whether deleted data persists in backups.
5) Any server-side caching or prefix/KV caches that may persist customer content and how they are controlled.
6) Whether hosted inference ever trains or fine-tunes on customer data by default.
7) Auditability: retention of audit logs, access to logs by Redwood staff, and available export options.

We appreciate concise, numbered responses we can paste into our vendor assessment. Attaching the sheet: Acme_Security_QA.xlsx.

Thanks,
Julia Santos
Security Analyst, Acme Corp


From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Hi Julia — thanks for sending this over and for the structured list. I'm attaching our standard DPA excerpt and a filled starter for your sheet (see attachments). Below is a high-level summary; Rishi (security/infra) will follow up with the precise, question-by-question answers for your questionnaire so you have an authoritative technical response to paste into your assessment.

High level:
- Residency: Customers can select a primary serving region for hosted API (US, EU). Requests routed to the chosen region for inference and short-term persistence; no cross-region replication of request payloads unless explicitly enabled for a specific enterprise contract.
- Retention: By default, we retain request/response content and associated request metadata for a short troubleshooting window. Customers may opt-out at the account level (disabling persistence) or pick a custom retention period via account settings or contract.
- Deletion: We support deletion-on-request at the record and account level. We aim to remove persisted records from primary storage within a bounded operational window; backups have a separate lifecycle (details to follow).
- Caching: Runtime uses memory-backed KV/prefix caches for latency; those caches are not used for long-term retention but some aggregate telemetry may be kept.
- Training: Redwood does not use hosted customers' production request/response content to train or fine-tune models by default.

I'll let Rishi provide the detailed Q/A that maps directly to your spreadsheet cells. If you need a legal contact for DPA/contract redlines, loop in procurement@redwood.com; Marissa is on copy and can help with the DPA/contract path.

Subject: RE: Redwood Hosted API — data handling questionnaire (detailed answers)

Hi Julia — following Kimberly's note, below are question-by-question answers you can copy into the spreadsheet. Where applicable I call out configuration options and timelines. If you'd like, we can also provide a redacted export of sample logs to demonstrate schema.

Question 1 — Data residency (where data is stored):
- Options: Customers may pick a primary region for hosted inference from our available regions: us-east-1 (North America) or eu-west-1 (Europe).
- Default: New accounts created via the public portal default to us-east-1 unless the signup flow or sales process requests EU residency.
- Routing: Inference executes and any transient persistence (see Q2) happens in the selected region. For enterprise contracts we can bind the control plane and telemetry to the customer VPC/region.

Question 2 — Default retention windows (inputs, outputs, metadata, debug logs):
- Request/response payloads (inputs/outputs): Default retention is 7 days for troubleshooting and billing reconciliation.
- Request metadata (timestamps, model id, latency, status codes): Retained 30 days by default for analytics and debugging.
- Debug logs and operator-facing traces: Retained 30 days by default; access is restricted via RBAC.
- Embeddings/derived artifacts: If a customer requests persistent embedding storage via our embeddings endpoint, those artifacts are retained per the customer's configured retention policy (default 90 days) — otherwise we do not persist embeddings beyond the request processing window.
- Customers can change retention at the account level to any value between 0 (no persistence) and 3650 days via account settings or via contract for enterprise accounts.

Question 3 — Deletion-on-request (mechanism & timeline):
- One-off record deletion: Customers may submit a deletion request via the Console or API (DELETE /v1/records/{id}). We remove records from primary store within 72 hours and confirm completion via webhook or console notification.
- Account-level purge: Customers requesting a full-account purge trigger an orchestrated deletion run; primary data removed within 7 calendar days.
- Verification: Deletion operations are recorded in an audit log entry; we provide a deletion report on request.

Question 4 — Backups and snapshots:
- Backups: We take encrypted daily snapshots of primary stores for disaster recovery. Snapshots are retained for 30 days by default and are stored encrypted in the same region; they are not accessible for normal query.
- Deleted data in backups: Following an account or record deletion, snapshots created before the deletion may still contain copies until the snapshot retention window expires. For customers requiring shorter backup retention or immediate scrub from backups, we include contractual options (e.g., shorter snapshot retention, locked key rotation, or dedicated retention processes) in enterprise agreements.

Question 5 — Server-side caching and KV caches:
- Runtime caches (in-memory KV/prefix caches): Used to accelerate repeated prefixes and reduce per-token cost. These caches are memory-resident and ephemeral; they are not written to durable storage by default.
- Control: Cache TTLs and whether a request is eligible for caching are configurable per account and can be disabled via the account flag `disable_runtime_caching` for compliance-sensitive customers.

Question 6 — Use of customer data for training/fine-tuning:
- Default policy: We do not use hosted customer production data to train or fine-tune shared models unless the customer explicitly opts in with an explicit contract clause.
- Enterprise exceptions: If fine-tuning or training on customer data is requested, it will be executed in a dedicated, opt-in environment with explicit data handling controls and retention windows stated in the SOW.

Question 7 — Audit logs and staff access:
- Audit logs: Administrative and access audit logs are retained 365 days by default (configurable for enterprise customers).
- Staff access: Access to production data is strictly controlled. Engineers require an approved access request via our access workflow; all access is time-limited and logged.
- Exports: Customers can export logs and records via the Console or API (CSV/JSON) and we can provide scheduled exports into a customer-owned S3 bucket for long-term retention under an enterprise agreement.

Additional controls and notes:
- Data-at-rest: All persisted data (primary and backup) is encrypted at rest using customer-managed keys (KMS) for enterprise plans; default managed keys are used for self-serve accounts.
- Data-in-transit: TLS 1.2+ enforced across the API surface.
- Redaction: Customers may enable automatic input redaction (PII masking) at the request level.

If you want these answers in the exact spreadsheet cells, I can paste them into Acme_Security_QA.xlsx and return it (I've attached a completed version: acme-answers-20261115.xlsx). Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you want to walk through any item.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
